calls.prompt:
Create ONE 2D fighting-game CHARACTER REFERENCE SHEET of Gorvax (the Chimera Engine), an ORIGINAL character for an original
indie fighting game. It must NOT resemble any existing anime, manga, game or film character.

The FIRST attached image is the approved HOUSE STYLE (another character of this game): copy its rendering exactly - the same
premium high-detail anime fighting-game sprite style, line work, cel shading, metal highlights, proportions, scale and the
same kind of sheet layout - but draw Gorvax, NOT the character shown there. The SECOND attached image is Gorvax's portrait:
match the face, hair, colours and costume from it.

THE CHARACTER:
A hulking, hunched chimera-engine warrior: enormous and heavy-boned, shoulders far wider than his head, a low forward-leaning stance. Head: a lion-like skull with a tawny muzzle of short fur, a dark iron brow plate, two glowing RED eyes deep under the brow, a snarl of long ivory fangs with thin steam venting from the jaw, and two curved dark goat HORNS sweeping back from the crown. A thick MANE of black riveted cables with tarnished BRASS rings falls from the skull over the shoulders and back. Armour: scuffed DARK IRON-GREY plates over chest and shoulders, brass-riveted stacked pauldrons, a black leather harness, brass-trimmed greaves and black boots. A segmented iron SERPENT tail trails low behind him, its links edged dull red. WEAPON: an ENGINE-HAMMER, a dark iron piston shaft as long as his body from hip to head with two brass collars, ending in a squat iron block as big as his chest, with a glowing red core in its face and a riveted brass band. Always held in BOTH hands: right hand low near the butt, left hand above it, the head out in front. Effects and weapon trails: RED-ORANGE embers, steam and sparks with a crimson glow.

ART STYLE: Premium, high-detail anime 2D fighting-game sprite art: the look of a carefully hand-pixelled character sprite rendered at high resolution - crisp deliberate dark outlines (not thick black cartoon lines), cel shading with three to four tones per material, bright specular highlights on metal, a cool rim light, an expressive face with a clear eye, anatomically correct hands with readable fingers, convincing anime anatomy, fluid hair and cloth that follow the motion. Exactly the rendering, palette and level of detail of the attached reference sheet. Not vector art, not blurry, not chibi, no photorealism.

SHEET CONTENT (transparent background, image 1536x1024, no text, no labels, no grid lines, every figure separate):
- top row: full-body neutral stance facing right; a combat stance with the hammer ready; a lumbering walking pose; a charging run; a leaping jump with the hammer back; a close-up of the engine-hammer head
- middle rows: six attack poses: two heavy overhead hammer smashes, a wide sideways hammer sweep, a ground slam with cracked earth, an airborne hammer swing, a Blood Frenzy rage pose; red embers and steam in each
- bottom row: guard with the hammer across the body, hit reaction, knocked down, victory pose with the hammer planted, the Blood Frenzy aura at full force
Every figure faces RIGHT (three-quarter side view like the house style), the same scale (standing height about 240 px), feet on
the same ground line within each row.

  (standing height about 399 px from heel to crown, even if a pose is crouched or stretched); the feet rest on the same invisible ground line
  31 px above the bottom edge of the cell (airborne frames are drawn at the SAME place in the cell -
  the game moves the character - just with the airborne pose); the torso stays about 138 px from the cell's
  left edge so a weapon has room in front.
- Nothing (weapon, cape, hair, effects) may cross into a neighbouring cell: keep a clear margin of 8 px at every cell edge, shorten
  the weapon's foreshortening or angle it if needed.
- Consecutive frames are ANIMATION FRAMES of one continuous motion: keep the costume, armour plates, weapon design, hair shape and
  colours identical between frames; only the pose changes.

THIS SHEET: Stance and footwork
  1. combat idle loop 1: fighting stance, weapon ready, knees bent, weight centred
  2. combat idle loop 2: the same stance breathing in, shoulders slightly raised, cape and hair drifting
  3. combat idle loop 3: the same stance at the top of the breath
  4. combat idle loop 4: the same stance breathing out, settling back toward frame 1
  5. standing guard: weapon raised across the body to block, braced, chin down
  6. crouch: low crouch on bent knees, weapon held low and ready (a crouching guard posture)
  7. skid: braking hard from a run, front foot planted forward, body leaning back, cape swinging forward
  8. landing: absorbing a landing from a jump, deep knee bend, one hand low for balance, cape still settling
Character-specific notes for this sheet: The mane cables and the steam from the jaw sway and drift with each breath; the hammer head stays low and steady in both hands.
